sanskrit: vajraṃ gṛhītvā ca puraṃdara tvaṃ; saṃprāhārṣīś cyavanasyātighoram sa te vipraḥ saha vajreṇa bāhum; apāgṛhṇāt tapasā jātamanyuḥ
english: And you, Puraṃdara, took up the thunderbolt and hurled it most terribly at Cyavana; but that brahman, his wrath born of austerity, seized your arm together with the very thunderbolt and held it fast.

sanskrit: tato roṣāt sarvato ghorarūpaṃ; sapatnaṃ te janayām āsa bhūyaḥ madaṃ nāmāsuraṃ viśvarūpaṃ; yaṃ tvaṃ dṛṣṭvā cakṣuṣī saṃnyamīlaḥ
english: Then out of fury he brought into being a rival for you, dreadful of form on every side, an asura named Mada of all-pervading shape, at the mere sight of whom you shut your eyes.

sanskrit: hanur ekā jagatīsthā tathaikā; divaṃ gatā mahato dānavasya sahasraṃ dantānāṃ śatayojanānāṃ; sutīkṣṇānāṃ ghorarūpaṃ babhūva
english: One jaw of that mighty dānava rested upon the earth, the other reached to heaven; a thousand teeth he had, each a hundred yojanas long, exceedingly sharp, of dreadful aspect.

sanskrit: vṛttāḥ sthūlā rajatastambhavarṇā; daṃṣṭrāś catasro dve śate yojanānām sa tvāṃ dantān vidaśann abhyadhāvaj; jighāṃsayā śūlam udyamya ghoram
english: His four tusks were round and massive, the color of pillars of silver, two hundred yojanas in length; gnashing his teeth he rushed upon you, raising a terrible spear in his desire to slay.

sanskrit: apaśyas tvaṃ taṃ tadā ghorarūpaṃ; sarve tv anye dadṛśur darśanīyam yasmād bhītaḥ prāñjalis tvaṃ maharṣim; āgacchethāḥ śaraṇaṃ dānavaghna
english: You could not bear to look upon that one of dreadful form, though all the others gazed upon him as upon a thing of wonder; and out of fear of him you came, slayer of dānavas, with palms joined, to take refuge with the great sage.

sanskrit: kṣatrād evaṃ brahmabalaṃ garīyo; na brahmataḥ kiṃ cid anyad garīyaḥ so 'haṃ jānan brahmatejo yathāvan; na saṃvartaṃ gantum icchāmi śakra
english: Thus the power of the brahman is mightier than that of the kṣatriya; there is nothing whatever mightier than the brahman. Knowing as I do the splendor of the brahman aright, I have no wish, O Śakra, to go against Saṃvarta.

sanskrit: indra uvāca evam etad brahmabalaṃ garīyo; na brahmataḥ kiṃ cid anyad garīyaḥ āvikṣitasya tu balaṃ na mṛṣye; vajram asmai prahariṣyāmi ghoram
english: Indra said: True it is that the power of the brahman is mightier, and that nothing whatever is mightier than the brahman; yet the might of Āvikṣita's son I will not endure—upon him I shall hurl the terrible thunderbolt.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra prahito gaccha maruttaṃ; saṃvartena sahitaṃ taṃ vadasva bṛhaspatiṃ tvam upaśikṣasva rājan; vajraṃ vā te prahariṣyāmi ghoram
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, go as my envoy and say to Marutta, who stands together with Saṃvarta: O king, accept Bṛhaspati for your priest, or else I shall hurl the terrible thunderbolt upon you.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tato gatvā dhṛtarāṣṭro narendraṃ; provācedaṃ vacanaṃ vāsavasya gandharvaṃ māṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ nibodha; tvām āgataṃ vaktukāmaṃ narendra
english: Vyāsa said: Then the gandharva Dhṛtarāṣṭra went and spoke to the king these words of Vāsava: Know me, O king, to be the gandharva Dhṛtarāṣṭra, come to you with a message to deliver.

sanskrit: aindraṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇu me rājasiṃha; yat prāha lokādhipatir mahātmā bṛhaspatiṃ yājakaṃ tvaṃ vṛṇīṣva; vajraṃ vā te prahariṣyāmi ghoram vacaś ced etan na kariṣyase me; prāhaitad etāvad acintyakarmā
english: Hear from me, lion among kings, the word of Indra which the great-souled lord of the worlds has spoken: Choose Bṛhaspati for your officiating priest, or else I shall hurl the terrible thunderbolt upon you; if you will not do this my bidding—so much has he of inconceivable deeds declared.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca tvaṃ caivaitad vettha puraṃdaraś ca; viśvedevā vasavaś cāśvinau ca mitradrohe niṣkṛtir vai yathaiva; nāstīti lokeṣu sadaiva vādaḥ
english: Marutta said: You yourself know this, and Puraṃdara too, the Viśvedevas, the Vasus, and the two Aśvins—that for treachery to a friend there is no expiation; such has ever been the saying in the worlds.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir yājayitā mahendraṃ; devaśreṣṭhaṃ vajrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭham saṃvarto māṃ yājayitādya rājan; na te vākyaṃ tasya vā rocayāmi
english: Let Bṛhaspati officiate for great Indra, the best of the gods, the foremost of the wielders of the thunderbolt; but Saṃvarta shall officiate for me this day, O king. Neither your word nor his is to my liking.

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca ghoro nādaḥ śrūyate vāsavasya; nabhastale garjato rājasiṃha vyaktaṃ vajraṃ mokṣyate te mahendraḥ; kṣemaṃ rājaṃś cintyatām eṣa kālaḥ
english: The gandharva said: A terrible roar is heard, lion among kings—the roar of Vāsava thundering in the vault of the sky. Surely great Indra is about to loose the thunderbolt upon you. Think now, O king, of your safety; this is the moment.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca ity evam ukto dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājā; śrutvā nādaṃ nadato vāsavasya taponityaṃ dharmavidāṃ variṣṭhaṃ; saṃvartaṃ taṃ jñāpayām āsa kāryam
english: Vyāsa said: Thus addressed by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and hearing the roar of the thundering Vāsava, the king made known the matter to Saṃvarta—that one ever devoted to austerity, the foremost of those who know the dharma.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca imam aśmānaṃ plavamānam ārād; adhvā dūraṃ tena na dṛśyate 'dya prapadye 'haṃ śarma viprendra tvattaḥ; prayaccha tasmād abhayaṃ vipramukhya
english: Marutta said: I behold yonder, floating near, a great mass like a stone, and by it the path ahead is hidden from view. I seek shelter, foremost of brahmans, from you; grant me, best of brahmans, refuge from that peril.

sanskrit: ayam āyāti vai vajrī diśo vidyotayan daśa amānuṣeṇa ghoreṇa sadasyās trāsitā hi naḥ
english: Here comes the wielder of the thunderbolt, lighting up the ten directions; by his dreadful, more-than-human form our priests at the sacrifice are stricken with terror.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca bhayaṃ śakrād vyetu te rājasiṃha; praṇotsye 'haṃ bhayam etat sughoram saṃstambhinyā vidyayā kṣipram eva; mā bhais tvam asmād bhava cāpi pratītaḥ
english: Saṃvarta said: Let your fear of Śakra depart, lion among kings; this most dreadful terror I shall straightway drive away by the spell of immobilizing power. Be not afraid of this, and be of good cheer.

sanskrit: ahaṃ saṃstambhayiṣyāmi mā bhais tvaṃ śakrato nṛpa sarveṣām eva devānāṃ kṣapitāny āyudhāni me
english: I will hold them fast and bound; fear not Śakra, O king. By me the weapons of all the gods can be made of no avail.

sanskrit: diśo vajraṃ vrajatāṃ vāyur etu; varṣaṃ bhūtvā nipatatu kānaneṣu āpaḥ plavantv antarikṣe vṛthā ca; saudāminī dṛśyatāṃ mā bibhas tvam
english: Let the thunderbolt wander off to the quarters of the sky, let the wind come, let it fall as rain upon the forests; let the waters drift idly in the air, let the lightning be seen flashing—but you, fear not.

sanskrit: atho vahnis trātu vā sarvatas te; kāmaṃ varṣaṃ varṣatu vāsavo vā vajraṃ tathā sthāpayatāṃ ca vāyur; mahāghoraṃ plavamānaṃ jalaughaiḥ
english: Or let fire guard you on every side; let Vāsava rain his rain as he pleases; and let the wind hold fast the thunderbolt, most dreadful as it floats amid floods of water.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca ghoraḥ śabdaḥ śrūyate vai mahāsvano; vajrasyaiṣa sahito mārutena ātmā hi me pravyathate muhur muhur; na me svāsthyaṃ jāyate cādya vipra
english: Marutta said: A terrible sound is heard, a mighty roar—this is the thunderbolt joined with the wind; my heart trembles again and again, and no ease comes to me this day, O brahman.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca vajrād ugrād vyetu bhayaṃ tavādya; vāto bhūtvā hanmi narendra vajram bhayaṃ tyaktvā varam anyaṃ vṛṇīṣva; kaṃ te kāmaṃ tapasā sādhayāmi
english: Saṃvarta said: Let your fear of the fierce thunderbolt depart this day; becoming the wind myself, O king, I strike down the thunderbolt. Set fear aside and choose some other boon: what desire of yours shall I accomplish by my austerity?

sanskrit: marutta uvāca indraḥ sākṣāt sahasābhyetu vipra; havir yajñe pratigṛhṇātu caiva svaṃ svaṃ dhiṣṇyaṃ caiva juṣantu devāḥ; sutaṃ somaṃ pratigṛhṇantu caiva
english: Marutta said: Let Indra himself come forth at once, O brahman, and accept the oblation at the sacrifice; let the gods each take their own seats and receive the pressed soma.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca ayam indro haribhir āyāti rājan; devaiḥ sarvaiḥ sahitaḥ somapīthī mantrāhūto yajñam imaṃ mayādya; paśyasvainaṃ mantravisrastakāyam
english: Saṃvarta said: Here comes Indra with his bay steeds, O king, the soma-drinker, together with all the gods, summoned by my mantras to this sacrifice this day; behold him, his body drawn hither by the power of the spell.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tato devaiḥ sahito devarājo; rathe yuktvā tān harīn vājimukhyān āyād yajñam adhi rājñaḥ pipāsur; āvikṣitasyāprameyasya somam
english: Vyāsa said: Then the king of the gods, attended by the gods, having yoked to his chariot those bay horses, the foremost of steeds, came to the sacrifice of the immeasurable son of Āvikṣita, thirsting for the soma.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ sahitaṃ devasaṃghaiḥ; pratyudyayau sapurodhā maruttaḥ cakre pūjāṃ devarājāya cāgryāṃ; yathāśāstraṃ vidhivat prīyamāṇaḥ
english: As he came accompanied by the hosts of gods, Marutta with his priest went forth to meet him, and offered foremost worship to the king of the gods, according to scripture and rite, with gladness of heart.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca svāgataṃ te puruhūteha vidvan; yajño 'dyāyaṃ saṃnihite tvayīndra śośubhyate balavṛtraghna bhūyaḥ; pibasva somaṃ sutam udyataṃ mayā
english: Saṃvarta said: Welcome to you here, O learned Puruhūta; this sacrifice shines forth the more now that you are present, O Indra, slayer of Bala and Vṛtra. Drink the soma, pressed and held ready by me.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca śivena māṃ paśya namaś ca te 'stu; prāpto yajñaḥ saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ me ayaṃ yajñaṃ kurute me surendra; bṛhaspater avaro janmanā yaḥ
english: Marutta said: Look upon me with favor, and homage be to you; my sacrifice is achieved, my life is fruitful. This one performs my sacrifice for me, O lord of the gods—he who is younger than Bṛhaspati by birth.

sanskrit: indra uvāca jānāmi te gurum enaṃ tapodhanaṃ; bṛhaspater anujaṃ tigmatejasam yasyāhvānād āgato 'haṃ narendra; prītir me 'dya tvayi manuḥ pranaṣṭaḥ
english: Indra said: I know this teacher of yours, rich in austerity, the younger brother of Bṛhaspati, of keen splendor, at whose summons I have come, O king. My displeasure toward you is now gone; my favor rests upon you this day.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca yadi prītas tvam asi vai devarāja; tasmāt svayaṃ śādhi yajñe vidhānam svayaṃ sarvān kuru mārgān surendra; jānātv ayaṃ sarvalokaś ca deva
english: Saṃvarta said: If you are indeed pleased, O king of the gods, then ordain yourself the rite at this sacrifice; arrange yourself all its courses, O lord of the gods, that all the world may know it, O god.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca evam uktas tv āṅgirasena śakraḥ; samādideśa svayam eva devān sabhāḥ kriyantām āvasathāś ca mukhyāḥ; sahasraśaś citrabhaumāḥ samṛddhāḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Thus addressed by the son of Aṅgiras, Śakra himself gave command to the gods: Let assembly halls be made, and chief dwellings by the thousand, rich and with floors of varied splendor.

sanskrit: kḷptasthūṇāḥ kurutārohaṇāni; gandharvāṇām apsarasāṃ ca śīghram yeṣu nṛtyerann apsarasaḥ sahasraśaḥ; svargoddeśaḥ kriyatāṃ yajñavāṭaḥ
english: With pillars set in place, make ascents straightway for the gandharvas and the apsarases, where the apsarases by the thousand may dance; let the sacrificial enclosure be made to seem a very image of heaven.

sanskrit: ity uktās te cakrur āśu pratītā; divaukasaḥ śakravākyān narendra tato vākyaṃ prāha rājānam indraḥ; prīto rājan pūjayāno maruttam
english: Thus bidden, the dwellers in heaven did all this swiftly and gladly at Śakra's word, O king; then Indra, well pleased, spoke to the king, honoring Marutta.

sanskrit: eṣa tvayāham iha rājan sametya; ye cāpy anye tava pūrve narendrāḥ sarvāś cānyā devatāḥ prīyamāṇā; havis tubhyaṃ pratigṛhṇantu rājan
english: Here am I come together with you, O king, and the other kings, your forefathers, are here as well; let all the other deities too, well pleased, accept the oblation from you, O king.

sanskrit: āgneyaṃ vai lohitam ālabhantāṃ; vaiśvadevaṃ bahurūpaṃ virājan nīlaṃ cokṣāṇaṃ medhyam abhyālabhantāṃ; calac chiśnaṃ matpradiṣṭaṃ dvijendrāḥ
english: Let them sacrifice the red beast for Agni, and the many-formed offering for the Viśvedevas, O resplendent one; let the foremost of brahmans offer up the dark, pure bull of vigorous member that I have appointed.

sanskrit: tato yajño vavṛdhe tasya rājño; yatra devāḥ svayam annāni jahruḥ yasmiñ śakro brāhmaṇaiḥ pūjyamānaḥ; sadasyo 'bhūd dharimān devarājaḥ
english: Then that king's sacrifice grew great, wherein the gods themselves took up the food, and wherein Śakra, lord of the gods and master of the bay steeds, honored by the brahmans, sat as a member of the assembly.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvartaś cityagato mahātmā; yathā vahniḥ prajvalito dvitīyaḥ havīṃṣy uccair āhvayan devasaṃghāñ; juhāvāgnau mantravat supratītaḥ
english: Then the great-souled Saṃvarta, mounted upon the altar like a second blazing fire, summoning aloud the hosts of gods, poured the oblations into the flame with the proper mantras, full of confidence.

sanskrit: tataḥ pītvā balabhit somam agryaṃ; ye cāpy anye somapā vai divaukasaḥ sarve 'nujñātāḥ prayayuḥ pārthivena; yathājoṣaṃ tarpitāḥ prītimantaḥ
english: Then the slayer of Bala, having drunk the foremost soma, and the other soma-drinking dwellers of heaven as well, all of them, sated to their content and well pleased, took their leave of the king and departed.

sanskrit: tato rājā jātarūpasya rāśīn; pade pade kārayām āsa hṛṣṭaḥ dvijātibhyo visṛjan bhūri vittaṃ; rarāja vitteśa ivārihantā
english: Then the king, rejoicing, had heaps of gold piled up at every step, and bestowing abundant wealth upon the twice-born, that slayer of foes shone like the lord of riches himself.

sanskrit: tato vittaṃ vividhaṃ saṃnidhāya; yathotsāhaṃ kārayitvā ca kośam anujñāto guruṇā saṃnivṛtya; śaśāsa gām akhilāṃ sāgarāntām
english: Then, having gathered wealth of many kinds and filled his treasury to his utmost, and having taken his leave with his teacher's consent, he returned and ruled the whole earth to the bounds of the sea.

sanskrit: evaṃguṇaḥ saṃbabhūveha rājā; yasya kratau tat suvarṇaṃ prabhūtam tat tvaṃ samādāya narendra vittaṃ; yajasva devāṃs tarpayāno vidhānaiḥ
english: Such of qualities was that king, at whose sacrifice gold was so abundant. Take you that wealth, O king, and offer sacrifice, gladdening the gods with due observances.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājā pāṇḍavo hṛṣṭarūpaḥ; śrutvā vākyaṃ satyavatyāḥ sutasya manaś cakre tena vittena yaṣṭuṃ; tato 'mātyair mantrayām āsa bhūyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the Pāṇḍava king, glad of countenance, hearing the words of the son of Satyavatī, set his mind upon sacrificing with that wealth; and thereupon he took counsel again with his ministers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity ukte nṛpatau tasmin vyāsenādbhutakarmaṇā vāsudevo mahātejās tato vacanam ādade
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the king had been thus addressed by Vyāsa of wondrous deeds, then Vāsudeva of great splendor took up the discourse.

sanskrit: taṃ nṛpaṃ dīnamanasaṃ nihatajñātibāndhavam upaplutam ivādityaṃ sadhūmam iva pāvakam
english: That king, downcast in mind, his kinsmen and friends slain, was like the sun in eclipse, like a fire wrapped in smoke.

sanskrit: nirviṇṇamanasaṃ pārthaṃ jñātvā vṛṣṇikulodvahaḥ āśvāsayan dharmasutaṃ pravaktum upacakrame
english: Knowing the son of Pṛthā to be despondent in mind, the upholder of the Vṛṣṇi line, consoling the son of Dharma, began to speak.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca sarvaṃ jihmaṃ mṛtyupadam ārjavaṃ brahmaṇaḥ padam etāvāñ jñānaviṣayaḥ kiṃ pralāpaḥ kariṣyati
english: Vāsudeva said: All that is crooked is the abode of death; uprightness is the abode of Brahman. Such, and no more, is the whole province of knowledge. What will idle lamenting avail?

sanskrit: naiva te niṣṭhitaṃ karma naiva te śatravo jitāḥ kathaṃ śatruṃ śarīrastham ātmānaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: Your work is not yet finished, nor are your enemies conquered. How is it that you do not perceive the enemy that dwells within your own body—your own self?

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi yathādharmaṃ yathāśrutam indrasya saha vṛtreṇa yathā yuddham avartata
english: On this I will relate to you, according to dharma and according to what I have heard, how the battle of Indra with Vṛtra came to pass.

sanskrit: vṛtreṇa pṛthivī vyāptā purā kila narādhipa dṛṣṭvā sa pṛthivīṃ vyāptāṃ gandhasya viṣaye hṛte dharāharaṇadurgandho viṣayaḥ samapadyata
english: Of old, O king, the earth was pervaded by Vṛtra, so it is told. Seeing the earth thus pervaded, and the province of smell carried off, there arose a foul stench—the province that came of the earth's being seized.

sanskrit: śatakratuś cukopātha gandhasya viṣaye hṛte vṛtrasya sa tataḥ kruddho vajraṃ ghoram avāsṛjat
english: Then the lord of a hundred sacrifices grew wroth at the carrying off of the province of smell, and in his anger he let loose the terrible thunderbolt upon Vṛtra.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno vajreṇa pṛthivyāṃ bhūritejasā viveśa sahasaivāpo jagrāha viṣayaṃ tataḥ
english: Being smitten by the thunderbolt of vast power, he straightway entered into the waters, abandoning the earth, and seized then the province of the waters.

sanskrit: vyāptāsv athāpsu vṛtreṇa rase ca viṣaye hṛte śatakratur abhikruddhas tāsu vajram avāsṛjat
english: When the waters had been pervaded by Vṛtra, and the province of taste carried off, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, sore angered, loosed the thunderbolt upon them.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno vajreṇa salile bhūritejasā viveśa sahasā jyotir jagrāha viṣayaṃ tataḥ
english: Being smitten in the water by the thunderbolt of vast power, he straightway entered into light, and seized then the province of light.

sanskrit: vyāpte jyotiṣi vṛtreṇa rūpe 'tha viṣaye hṛte śatakratur abhikruddhas tatra vajram avāsṛjat
english: When light had been pervaded by Vṛtra, and the province of form carried off, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, sore angered, loosed the thunderbolt there.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno vajreṇa subhṛśaṃ bhūritejasā viveśa sahasā vāyuṃ jagrāha viṣayaṃ tataḥ
english: Being smitten hard by the thunderbolt of vast power, he straightway entered into the wind, and seized then the province of wind.

sanskrit: vyāpte vāyau tu vṛtreṇa sparśe 'tha viṣaye hṛte śatakratur abhikruddhas tatra vajram avāsṛjat
english: When the wind had been pervaded by Vṛtra, and the province of touch carried off, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, sore angered, loosed the thunderbolt there.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno vajreṇa tasminn amitatejasā ākāśam abhidudrāva jagrāha viṣayaṃ tataḥ
english: Being smitten therein by the thunderbolt of measureless power, he rushed into the ether, and seized then its province.

sanskrit: ākāśe vṛtrabhūte ca śabde ca viṣaye hṛte śatakratur abhikruddhas tatra vajram avāsṛjat
english: When the ether had become Vṛtra, and the province of sound carried off, the lord of a hundred sacrifices, sore angered, loosed the thunderbolt there.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno vajreṇa tasminn amitatejasā viveśa sahasā śakraṃ jagrāha viṣayaṃ tataḥ
english: Being smitten therein by the thunderbolt of measureless power, he straightway entered into Śakra himself, and seized then his province.

sanskrit: tasya vṛtragṛhītasya mohaḥ samabhavan mahān rathaṃtareṇa taṃ tāta vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyabodhayat
english: As he was thus seized by Vṛtra, a great bewilderment came over him; but Vasiṣṭha, my son, roused him again to consciousness with the Rathaṃtara hymn.

sanskrit: tato vṛtraṃ śarīrasthaṃ jaghāna bharatarṣabha śatakratur adṛśyena vajreṇetīha naḥ śrutam
english: Then the lord of a hundred sacrifices slew Vṛtra, who dwelt within his body, O bull of the Bharatas, with an unseen thunderbolt—so have we heard it here.

sanskrit: idaṃ dharmarahasyaṃ ca śakreṇoktaṃ maharṣiṣu ṛṣibhiś ca mama proktaṃ tan nibodha narādhipa
english: This secret of dharma was declared by Śakra among the great sages, and by the seers it was told to me; learn it now, O king.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca dvividho jāyate vyādhiḥ śārīro mānasas tathā parasparaṃ tayor janma nirdvaṃdvaṃ nopalabhyate
english: Vāsudeva said: Disease arises of two kinds, of the body and of the mind; the one is born of the other, and neither is found to arise wholly apart from its fellow.

sanskrit: śarīre jāyate vyādhiḥ śārīro nātra saṃśayaḥ mānaso jāyate vyādhir manasy eveti niścayaḥ
english: The disease of the body is born in the body, of that there is no doubt; and the disease of the mind, it is determined, is born in the mind alone.

sanskrit: śītoṣṇe caiva vāyuś ca guṇā rājañ śarīrajāḥ teṣāṃ guṇānāṃ sāmyaṃ cet tad āhuḥ svasthalakṣaṇam uṣṇena bādhyate śītaṃ śītenoṣṇaṃ ca bādhyate
english: Cold, heat, and wind, O king, are the qualities born of the body; when these qualities are in balance, that they call the mark of health. Cold is subdued by heat, and heat is subdued by cold.

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś ceti trayas tv ātmaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ teṣāṃ guṇānāṃ sāmyaṃ cet tad āhuḥ svasthalakṣaṇam teṣām anyatamotseke vidhānam upadiśyate
english: Goodness, passion, and darkness—these three are reckoned the qualities of the soul; when these qualities are in balance, that they call the mark of health. And when any one of them rises in excess, a remedy is prescribed for it.

sanskrit: harṣeṇa bādhyate śoko harṣaḥ śokena bādhyate kaś cid duḥkhe vartamānaḥ sukhasya smartum icchati kaś cit sukhe vartamāno duḥkhasya smartum icchati
english: Sorrow is subdued by joy, and joy is subdued by sorrow; one man, dwelling in misery, wishes to remember his happiness, while another, dwelling in happiness, wishes to remember his misery.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ na duḥkhī duḥkhasya na sukhī susukhasya vā smartum icchasi kaunteya diṣṭaṃ hi balavattaram
english: But you, O son of Kuntī, being neither now in misery would recall your misery, nor in deep happiness would recall your happiness—for fate is the stronger force.

sanskrit: atha vā te svabhāvo 'yaṃ yena pārthāvakṛṣyase dṛṣṭvā sabhāgatāṃ kṛṣṇām ekavastrāṃ rajasvalām miṣatāṃ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ na tat saṃsmartum icchasi
english: Or perhaps this is your very nature, by which you are drawn down, O Pārtha; for when you saw Kṛṣṇā brought into the assembly hall, in a single garment, in her courses, before the very eyes of the Pāṇḍavas—that you do not wish to remember.

sanskrit: pravrājanaṃ ca nagarād ajinaiś ca vivāsanam mahāraṇyanivāsaś ca na tasya smartum icchasi
english: The banishment from the city, the sending forth clad in deerskins, and the dwelling in the great forest—of that you do not wish to remember.

sanskrit: jaṭāsurāt parikleśaś citrasenena cāhavaḥ saindhavāc ca parikleśo na tasya smartum icchasi
english: The affliction at the hands of Jaṭāsura, the combat with Citrasena, and the affliction from the king of the Sindhus—of that you do not wish to remember.

sanskrit: punar ajñātacaryāyāṃ kīcakena padā vadhaḥ yājñasenyās tadā pārtha na tasya smartum icchasi
english: And again, during the time of concealment, the kicking of Yājñasenī by Kīcaka—of that too, O Pārtha, you do not wish to remember.

sanskrit: yac ca te droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ yuddham āsīd ariṃdama manasaikena yoddhavyaṃ tat te yuddham upasthitam tasmād abhyupagantavyaṃ yuddhāya bharatarṣabha
english: The war you waged against Droṇa and Bhīṣma, O subduer of foes—even such a war is now at hand for you, to be fought with the mind alone; therefore you must take it up for battle, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: param avyaktarūpasya paraṃ muktvā svakarmabhiḥ yatra naiva śaraiḥ kāryaṃ na bhṛtyair na ca bandhubhiḥ ātmanaikena yoddhavyaṃ tat te yuddham upasthitam
english: It is the highest war, against that whose form is unmanifest, won by setting aside the highest through one's own deeds—wherein there is no need of arrows, nor of servants, nor of kinsmen; it must be fought with the self alone, and that war is now at hand for you.

sanskrit: tasminn anirjite yuddhe kām avasthāṃ gamiṣyasi etaj jñātvā tu kaunteya kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi
english: Should that war remain unwon, to what state will you come? But once you have understood this, O son of Kuntī, you will have accomplished your purpose.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhiṃ viniścitya bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim pitṛpaitāmahe vṛtte śādhi rājyaṃ yathocitam
english: Having resolved upon this wisdom—the coming and the going of all beings—rule the kingdom fittingly, in the way of your fathers and forefathers.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca na bāhyaṃ dravyam utsṛjya siddhir bhavati bhārata śārīraṃ dravyam utsṛjya siddhir bhavati vā na vā
english: Vāsudeva said: Not by casting off outward possessions does perfection come, O Bhārata; by casting off the body's own substance, perfection may come—or it may not.

sanskrit: bāhyadravyavimuktasya śārīreṣu ca gṛdhyataḥ yo dharmo yat sukhaṃ caiva dviṣatām astu tat tathā
english: For one who has renounced outward possessions yet still hankers after things of the body—whatever his dharma, whatever his happiness, let that be the lot of our enemies.

sanskrit: dvyakṣaras tu bhaven mṛtyus tryakṣaraṃ brahma śāśvatam mameti dvyakṣaro mṛtyur na mameti ca śāśvatam
english: Of two syllables is death, of three the eternal Brahman: 'mine' (mama), of two syllables, is death; 'not mine' (na mama) is the eternal.

sanskrit: brahma mṛtyuś ca tau rājann ātmany eva vyavasthitau adṛśyamānau bhūtāni yodhayetām asaṃśayam
english: Brahman and death, O king—both of these are established within the self alone; unseen, they set all beings to war with one another, beyond all doubt.
